submissions.findingTextShort: PMID 41875856 is a profile of botanist Noni Franklin-Tong, not evidence about the Noni plant.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 41875856 / DOI 10.1016/j.cub.2026.01.057 is a Current Biology profile/interview of botanist Noni Franklin-Tong. The token 'Noni' refers to a person's given name rather than Morinda citrifolia, a Noni preparation, or any botanical intervention. This source cannot semantically support efficacy, safety, mechanism, preparation, or recommendation claims for the Noni herb profile.
submissions.usageContext: Source-integrity quarantine only; no Morinda citrifolia intervention or botanical evidence is present.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: The entity mismatch is direct. This draft record documents a semantic false positive and must not itself become a clinical evidence receipt. Canonical removal requires governed repair.

submissions.findingTextShort: PMID 37313239 is a resmetirom/NASH review and is unrelated to Morinda citrifolia or Noni use.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: PMID 37313239 / DOI 10.17925/EE.2023.19.1.60 reviews resmetirom, a thyroid-hormone-receptor-beta agonist developed for nonalcoholic fatty liver disease and nonalcoholic steatohepatitis. It does not evaluate Morinda citrifolia, Noni fruit, Noni juice, Noni polysaccharides, or any Noni intervention and therefore cannot support the Noni profile.
submissions.usageContext: Source-integrity quarantine only; pharmacologic NASH review unrelated to Noni.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: The intervention/entity mismatch is direct. Canonical removal should occur through governed semantic repair, not silent reassignment.

submissions.findingTextShort: A 2026 fermented-Noni-polysaccharide RCT had null primary mITT NK-cell comparisons and no significant URTI-incidence benefit.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A randomized double-blind placebo-controlled trial enrolled 100 adults aged 40 to under 75 years with recurrent upper respiratory tract infections and tested fermented Noni polysaccharides at 975 mg/day for 8 weeks. In the prespecified modified-intention-to-treat/full-analysis set, between-group differences in NK-cell activity at all three effector-to-target ratios did not reach statistical significance. Prespecified per-protocol sensitivity analyses were significant at two ratios, selected cytokine biomarkers increased, but upper-respiratory-tract-infection incidence did not differ significantly between groups. The primary analysis therefore does not establish clinical infection-prevention efficacy.
submissions.populationContext: One hundred adults with at least two URTIs in the prior year; 84 were included in the mITT/FAS and 81 in the per-protocol set.
submissions.usageContext: Fermented Morinda citrifolia polysaccharide extract, 975 mg/day for eight weeks; preparation-specific evidence only.
submissions.safetyContext: No serious adverse events or treatment-related discontinuations were reported during the eight-week trial, which does not establish rare-event or long-term safety.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: The trial was retrospectively registered after completion. Product/funding affiliations included NSTbio and Atomy. Favorable per-protocol and cytokine findings must not overwrite the null primary mITT biomarker comparisons or null URTI-incidence result. The source remains draft-only until registry and semantic-attestation governance are complete.

submissions.findingTextShort: A Noni safety/pharmacology review found clinical benefit evidence historically sparse and urged continued vigilance around liver-safety reports.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: A review of Morinda citrifolia fruit phytochemistry, pharmacology, safety, and health claims concluded that experimental pharmacology was substantially richer than clinical evidence and that the clinical relevance of preclinical findings remained uncertain. It also reviewed liver-safety concerns and noted that, despite prior toxicologic and regulatory assessments, continuing monitoring and vigilance were appropriate in light of hepatotoxicity case reports.
submissions.usageContext: Noni fruit and Noni-derived products; review-level evidence and safety context rather than a direct efficacy trial.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: This older review predates newer human trials and should be used as historical certainty/safety context, not as a freshness anchor or proof of either hepatotoxicity incidence or clinical efficacy. The source remains draft-only until registry and semantic-attestation governance are complete.

submissions.findingTextShort: Published hepatitis case reports after Noni-juice exposure are safety signals but do not establish population incidence or certain causality.
submissions.findingTextNormalized: Human case reports describe acute hepatitis occurring after several weeks of Noni juice exposure, with improvement after discontinuation in at least one report. These reports support retaining a liver-injury safety signal and the need for formulation/exposure context, but isolated case reports cannot quantify incidence, establish a universal causal relationship, or define a dose threshold for Noni-associated liver injury.
submissions.populationContext: Individual adult case reports rather than controlled population-level safety studies.
submissions.usageContext: Noni juice exposure; must not be generalized automatically to fermented polysaccharide extracts or every Morinda citrifolia preparation.
submissions.safetyContext: Signal-level hepatotoxicity evidence only; no incidence estimate or broad causal certainty.
submissions.uncertaintyNote: Case reports are vulnerable to confounding and cannot quantify risk magnitude. Preserve them as safety signals alongside regulatory/toxicologic assessments and newer controlled-trial tolerability data. This source remains draft-only until source governance is complete.
